newsitem.title: INDIA: India company law panel for derivatives, options.
newsitem.headline: India company law panel for derivatives, options.

text.p: A working group set up by the Indian government said on Monday that companies should be allowed to issue derivatives, options and quasi-equity instruments.

The report, which considered amendments to India's Company Law, said that foreign companies should be allowed to issue Indian depositary receipts (IDRs) on the lines of European global depositary receipts (GDRs) where the underlying security is the equity or any other security of the foreign company.
"Indian companies should be enabled to issue hybrids, derivatives, options, as well as shares and quasi-equity instruments with differential rights," the report said.
It said hybrids were a combination of securities including their derivatives or options. "Shares with differential rights" refer to differing voting and dividend rights, it said.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram set up the working group last year under the chairmanship of K. R. Chandratre, the then chairman of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India to present a report for public debate.

The expert committee said it recommended that foreign companies should be allowed to issue IDRs keeping in mind that over time India will get much more economically integrated with its South Asian neighbours and South-East Asian economies.
The panel said firms that issue GDRs or American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) must file with the Registrar of Companies in order that they are governed by the Companies Act.

It said the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) should issue guidelines for hybrids, derivatives, options and quasi-equity for corporations, while the Department of Company Affairs should do the same for private and unlisted firms.
